content.text: This tool provides an auto-updating generation widget for these jobs. Do not call job_display, show_generations, or show_generation_by_ids to display these jobs again, either before or after completion, unless the user explicitly requests a separate display. If you need to await completion, use jobs_wait with timeout_seconds <= 15. Use job_display only if the user explicitly requests a separate re-display of one specific job.

- adbdd1b7-703a-4290-92fc-1f1a1e3a396b  "Create ONE 15-second premium editorial website film, with SIX cleanly cut shots and visible, physically plausible movement. Use only the three supplied references. Reference 1 is an approved decorative silk-loop, amber-orb and travertine atelier, not a sold product. Reference 2 is the actual cream/apricot floral midi dress. Reference 3 is the actual ceramic storage-jar gallery; the front-left floral jar is the product anchor.

The previous attempt kept product identity but mainly enlarged still pictures. Correct that specifically: NO scale-only digital photo zoom, no frozen whole-frame holds, no slideshow transitions, no morphing. Make the movement happen inside the scene. Use controlled cloth motion, real depth parallax, changing light/reflection and precise rack focus. Keep the pace calm and photographic, not hectic.

Six-shot edit, exactly 15 seconds overall:
0–2 s: Atelier establishing shot. A short lateral camera dolly produces real parallax between the amber orb, plinth, silk loop and rear arch. The long silk tail completes one clearly visible slow soft wave, roughly a hand-width of displacement; the silk loop and its recognizable silhouette remain intact. Architecture, orb and plinth remain rigid. Warm window shadows move gently. Reframe the existing wide composition naturally into 3:4; do not stretch the arch or silk.
2–5 s: Full frontal dress shot in the supplied light studio. Both straps and the entire hem remain inside the frame with breathing room. Camera is locked; do not enlarge the whole image. A brief gentle airflow moves ONLY the existing lower skirt folds a few centimetres and lets them settle. The bodice, straps, neckline and waist seam remain stable. Printed blue/orange/red motifs stay attached to their original fabric areas during the fold movement; do not redraw or rearrange flowers. Keep the warm ivory/apricot base colour, silhouette and length.
5–7 s: Clean cut to a closer frontal view of the SAME existing dress bodice and waist from reference 2. This is a deliberate detail cut, not a moving crop or zoom. Preserve the visible original seams and exact conspicuous print positions. A soft moving side light reveals the existing fabric folds; no new texture, material claim, wearer, mannequin or view of the back.
7–10 s: Clean cut to the ceramic gallery. Camera fixed at the original near-frontal angle. Keep every jar, handle and lid stationary. The complete front-left floral jar remains visible, with its seated lid, knob, white handles, dark-brown rim, blue flower decoration and base. Keep the existing partial rightmost jar crop; do not reconstruct unseen sides or rims. A restrained focus pull from the nearer loose lid to the front-left jar and a moving soft reflection across its glaze create visible optical movement. No zoom, opening, hands, pouring, extra contents or functional claims.
10–12 s: Clean cut to a closer view of the existing front-left jar's floral body, rim and lid. Preserve its exact shape and recognizable blue pattern. Keep the jar stationary; show a gentle controlled light/reflection sweep, with a precise shallow-focus settle on the original blue decoration. Do not move the lid, redraw flowers or imply the photographed gallery is a purchased set.
12–15 s: Clean cut back to the atelier. Use a second short lateral dolly, with clearly visible silk-tail movement and stable orb/plinth/architecture. Resolve the motion toward a recognizable resting composition. End calmly; a seamless loop is optional and must not force a frozen shot.

Keep references strictly separated: atelier only in shots 1 and 6; dress only in shots 2 and 3; ceramic gallery only in shots 4 and 5. No objects or patterns crossing locations. The controlled independent scene motion is essential, while exact product identity takes priority. Product establishing shots show full product forms; detail shots crop intentionally only to verified visible features, never invent hidden parts.
Premium photographic realism, consistent cream/taupe and natural amber lighting, precise hard editorial cuts. Native portrait 3:4, no aggressive artificial zoom, no slideshow, no stock inserts, no extra objects. Silent: no music, voiceover or audio. No text, lettering, logos, captions or CTA burned into the video; website HTML supplies those. No invented features, materials, reviews or origin claims.
Additional fidelity safeguards: the dress detail is the same front-facing dress crop, with no new side/back surfaces, straps or folds that change its cut. The jar detail uses only source-visible front-left surfaces; focus changes only optical sharpness, never pattern geometry. Reflections travel only across the existing glaze, with no floating light objects. Animate only the existing silk tail/loop, with no added strands; the orb and its base remain fixed."

If the user requests a combined display of multiple generations, including jobs submitted through separate generate_* calls, collect all requested job IDs, wait for the complete set with jobs_wait, then call show_generation_by_ids with jobs: [{"index":0,"job_id":"<first actual job ID>"},{"index":1,"job_id":"<second actual job ID>"}, ...]. job_display accepts only one id: never pass ids to it or loop over it to show a group. Do not create an extra display when the existing generation widgets already satisfy the request.
